name: Crosscut
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: animation storyboard SPRITE SHEET for a pixel RPG, to be cut into an actual animated GIF. Input 1 is ONLY the immutable King character identity/palette reference. Input 2 is the exact massive greatsword shape/material reference.
Create one transparent PNG sprite sheet, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and FIVE ROWS, twenty equally spaced SQUARE CELLS, portrait aspect ratio 4:5, ideally 1536x1920. NO labels, lines, text, numbers, scenery, colored background or checkerboard artwork. Real alpha. The frames are read LEFT TO RIGHT per row, then row by row. Each row is one strike: column1 anticipation inherited directly from the last row's endpoint, column2 early moving sword/body, column3 contact/maximum slash, column4 follow-through connecting to the next row. These are consecutive ANIMATION FRAMES, NOT twenty independent poster poses. Make every consecutive blade position and body weight transfer readable with no random pose reset between strikes.
Lock King's spiky BLACK hair, red scarf, small pale face, dark slate-blue short tunic, brown shoulder leather/belt/gloves/boots, same body/costume design and colors throughout. Small compact chibi proportions, hard dark pixel contours, clear hand grip. The huge steel weapon remains the SAME long broad silver blade and dark fuller with the SAME brown handle throughout, blade ~1.7x standing body height, never stretching or becoming a katana. Rotating the sword is allowed, changing its shape is not. Always face the enemy on SCREEN RIGHT; torso can rotate during swings but no accidental character flip or random front-facing hero poster. Fixed slightly elevated 3/4 side RPG camera, no camera rotation.
Each square cell has identical registration. Character hips centered horizontally, foot ground baseline at 81% cell height; standing character height ~30% cell height. Jump moves body UP only from that planted baseline. Allow real leg/body shifts for stepping/rotation, keep scale and camera exact. Whole character, blade, slash and sparks MUST remain inside its OWN cell with at least 5% completely transparent margin on every edge. No cropping, neighboring-cell intrusion or disconnected floating sword. No glow rectangle. Pixel art with crisp intentionally chunky pixels, upper-left light, not vector ribbons, not smooth 3D, not glossy illustration. Use pale white/silver slash raster accents attached to the moving OUTER half of the blade, with negative space around King's face and hands. The effect follows each actual stroke's direction, builds during motion, flashes at contact, decays at endpoint. Effects must not obscure the character, no repeated flat giant white blob and no gold.
The deliverable is a motion concept sheet, not a designed game UI. Background fully transparent; no terrain or floor under any frame.
OPTION A: GROUNDED CROSSCUT. Five fluent strikes with planted feet, obvious torso/hip rotation and true weighty shoulder windup, two-hand power. NEW slash art: clean ivory-white crescents with charcoal-grey inner edge and only 2-3 tapered parallel streaks. Bold white at the cutting edge, large transparent inner center. Elegant hand-drawn pixel slashes with no cyan halo.
Row1: rear-shoulder loaded diagonal DOWNWARD forehand through enemy right, finishes with blade extended LOW RIGHT.
Row2: from that low right endpoint, a powerful reverse RISING BACKHAND up across the front, finishes HIGH RIGHT/overhead.
Row3: sword already overhead, compact hop then decisive VERTICAL DOWNWARD cleave, finishes tip down and forward RIGHT.
Row4: from low-right finish scoop diagonally UP AND OUT toward enemy right, finishes blade EXTENDED HIGH RIGHT and torso wound opposite.
Row5: BEGIN exactly from Row4's extended high-right finish; strike BACK THROUGH THE OPPOSITE diagonal across the enemy, ending low-left past King's body. This is a genuine return of the steel from its previous position, not replay of guard/windup, not throwing the sword, not rear enemy targeting. End with a relaxed low guard ready to wind behind the shoulder again. Slash form alternates '/' and '\\' with steel movement. Give the last stroke a crisp double-taper trail without changing weapon/character.

OPTION B: HEAVY BREAKER. Five POWERFUL two-handed strikes, exaggerated knees/hips compression and slower heavy acceleration, a memorable jump slam. Row1: wide shoulder-height HORIZONTAL forehand, large step into the enemy RIGHT, ends sword across lower-right front.

Row4: directly from raised blade launch a clear compact jumping OVERHEAD SLAM; column1 takeoff, column2 airborne raised sword, column3 sword impacts low RIGHT with a narrow vertical WHITE impact wedge and sparse ice-grey shards, column4 low landing crouch with blade at forward ground. DO NOT bury an unrelated white ring behind the player.
Row5: from the low landing endpoint, use the sword's recoil into a rising diagonal REBOUND CUT toward RIGHT; finish heavy steel laid across shoulder, proud stance. Distinct compact shock-fragment slash. Momentum comes from squash/weightshift and striking motion, not floating still poses. Last column settles into the carry which can load row1 again.

OPTION C: ROYAL WHIRL. Five confident almost-playful ONE-HANDED heavy-sword turns with clear foot pivots, hip lead, scarf motion, small aerial flourish. Different readable full-body sequence from the grounded crosscut and heavy two-hand breaker, same King identity. NEW slash artwork: layered SILVER and muted PALE VIOLET ghost crescents, 2-3 offset echoes and small star-like pixel glints. No opaque thick white donut, no gold, no neon fire, no huge orb. Trails follow steel, keep inner negative space.
Row1: relaxed one-hand carry loads from shoulder into diagonal down-right forehand, ends low right with free hand balancing.
Row2: maintain momentum into an ORBITAL SPIN sweep around waist: real 3/4 rear torso turn during pivot then screen-right facing returns, blade ends back left ready to rise. Row3: rising TURNING CUT from back-left across right enemy, feet pivot and tip finishes up-right above head. The free hand stays physically plausible.
Row4: compact HOP with a small corkscrew torso turn, descending DIAGONAL SLAM down-right, ends grounded sword extended at low-right, sparse silver-violet landing shard detail.
Row5: START at that SAME low-right landing endpoint and deliver an elegant BACKHAND RETURN up across the front, moving steel from its last position, finish high-left/shoulder carried with confident posture. Entire sequence should flow, not restart from idle for every hit. Vary trail silhouette per stroke while keeping cool restrained palette and clear blade grip.
